title: Split body contracts from a unary source
statement: Let $C,e$ be natural numbers, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a$ be one of its states, and let $B:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every Boolean word $s$, starting from state $a$ with empty output and each work tape holding the unary word of length $|s|+1$, the machine halts after $B(|s|)$ steps with output consisting of $C(|s|+1)^e$ ones and unchanged tape contents. Suppose also that $B(l)\le (C+1+5e)(l+1)^e+1$ for every natural number $l$. Then, on every Boolean input $w$, the combined split-search body reaches its anchored empty-candidate configuration within $K(|w|+1)^{e+1}$ steps, with no earlier visit to the anchor, where $K=(C+1+5e)2^e+45$. Moreover, for every Boolean word $s$ with $|s|\le |w|+1$, there is a positive $t\le K(|w|+1)^{e+1}$ such that, from the anchor with candidate $s$ on the first work tape and all other work tapes blank, no strictly intermediate positive time visits the anchor; at time $t$ it halts with the encoded prefix of $w$ of length $|s|$ and remaining suffix if $|s|+C(|s|+1)^e=|w|$, and otherwise returns to the anchor with candidate $s$ followed by one $1$ bit and all other work tapes blank.
